–Results–Scientists will either directly observe or will model using technology to collect data.–Data is any result of an experiment, and can be observational or numerical–Statistical Analysis is needed to determine if data results are statistically significant
–Conclusions –After analyzing results, determine if hypothesis is supported or not–Science is never ending; can lead to new questions–Findings reported to scientific community through reports, journals, presentations, etc. –Results must be replicable by scientific community
explanation: This slide details how scientific results and conclusions are handled. To gather data—defined as any result of an experiment, whether observational or numerical—scientists make direct observations or use technological models. Statistical analysis is required to establish whether the collected data are statistically significant. After analysis, conclusions are drawn regarding whether the hypothesis is supported. Science is a continuous process that often generates new questions. Finally, results are shared with the scientific community via reports, journals, and presentations, and the findings must be replicable by other researchers.

questions.q: What is the purpose of statistical analysis in scientific experiments?
opts: To determine if data results are statistically significant
To prove that hypotheses are absolute facts
questions.exp: The slide states: 'Statistical Analysis is needed to determine if data results are statistically significant'.

questions.q: Which of the following is a requirement for experimental findings reported to the scientific community?
opts: They must prove the hypothesis without any doubt.
They must be replicable by the scientific community.
They must only contain numerical data.
questions.exp: The text states: 'Results must be replicable by scientific community'.
